_comment: Per-bit rail swing (gamma) and CPA outcome as the secret block V is moved away from the attacker block G on the Raspberry Pi 5. Measured with the uncacheable barrier gadget (ARM_N_DSBSY) on DDR_VDD2_A. Source runs: crossbank_gamma.py (gamma probe, one allocation, G fixed) and crossbank_rho_compare.py / v11_cpa_crossbank.py (paired rho calibration and full CPA). Narrative record: docs/CROSSBANK_CPA.md.
conclusion: The binding requirement is channel co-location, not row or bank co-location. Different-bank/same-channel (78%) beats same-bank/different-row (56%) because a row-buffer conflict, not leaving the row, is what costs signal. Crossing to a different channel removes the shared DQ bus and the cross-term with it.
